evidence: The Fear and Greed Index sits at 77 ('Extreme Greed') for the second consecutive day, holding well above both the 7-day mean of 73.29 and the 30-day mean of 59.60. Sustained high sentiment reflects robust bullish momentum following the mid-October rally out of fear/neutral territory. While persistent extreme greed can occasionally foreshadow local profit-taking or mean-reversion pullbacks, short-term momentum during established risk-on phases modestly favors upward continuation over 24 hours. Accounting for heightened volatility and asymmetric downside risk at elevated sentiment levels, the probability of closing higher is set slightly above even odds at 0.52.
limitations: Fear and Greed is a lagging/coincident composite sentiment metric rather than a direct predictive leading indicator.
